# Global commands

Top-level commands

## commands

Read-only: list every command with its kind (read vs guarded-mutation), offline. Pass a group name to drill in for flags and args

```text
secopsctl commands [group]
```

```text
Walk the command tree and list every runnable command: its path, one-line
description, local flags, and KIND — `guarded-mutation` for commands that
carry the standard --dry-run/--yes live-mutation gate, `read` otherwise.

Without arguments: grouped catalog (compact). With a group name: detail
for that group's commands (flags, args).

Offline (no API call, no credentials) — the verb-level companion to
`secopsctl surfaces`, and the input for building per-command allowlists
for automation/agents.
```

## config

Set up the secopsctl config (~/.secopsctl/instance.yaml)

```text
secopsctl config [flags]
```

```text
Create or edit the instance config in an interactive form: click a field or
use ↑/↓ or Tab to move, edit in place, then click Save (or Cancel). The
mouse wheel moves through fields when the form is taller than the terminal.
The SOAR AppKey field is hidden. Flags set values directly;
--non-interactive (or non-terminal stdin) skips the form and writes flags +
current values.

Writes ~/.secopsctl/instance.yaml (0600), or the --config path if given.
The file may hold the SOAR AppKey in plaintext (v1); it is git-ignored and
never committed. At run time, real SECOPS_* env vars override the file. The
mintable OAuth/ADC SIEM token is never stored — `gcloud auth
application-default login` handles SIEM auth.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--customer-id` | string | - | SecOps customer ID (GUID) |
| `--force-ipv4` | bool | false | pin the network dialer to IPv4 (corporate-VPN / broken-IPv6 fix) |
| `--project-id` | string | - | GCP project ID |
| `--project-number` | string | - | GCP project number |
| `--region` | string | - | SecOps region (e.g. us, asia-southeast1) |
| `--show-path` | bool | false | print the resolved config file path and exit (no changes) |
| `--soar-app-key` | string | - | SOAR AppKey (avoid on shared shells — prefer the prompt) |
| `--soar-url` | string | - | SOAR host URL (e.g. https://<tenant>.siemplify-soar.com) |

**Examples**

```bash
# open the interactive setup form
  secopsctl config

  # set values non-interactively (e.g. in a script)
  secopsctl config --non-interactive \
      --project-id your-project-id --project-number 000000000000 \
      --region us --customer-id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

  # print the resolved config file path
  secopsctl config --show-path
```

## doctor

Validate config, auth, and API connectivity (read-only)

```text
secopsctl doctor
```

```text
doctor checks that secopsctl is correctly configured and can reach its
APIs. It validates the config file (existence, permissions, required fields),
acquires auth credentials, and makes one lightweight read-only call to the
SIEM plane and, when configured, the SOAR plane. It never mutates anything.
By default all health probes must finish within 10s; --timeout overrides that
doctor-wide deadline (0 disables it).
--json emits {ok, version, checks[]}.
```

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl doctor        # human-readable
  secopsctl doctor --json # machine-readable (CI / monitoring)
```

## drift

Read-only: report how live state has drifted from local files (CI gate)

```text
secopsctl drift [target...] [flags]
```

```text
Compare committed local files to live state across the reconcile surfaces
and report divergence (local-only +, changed ~, live-only -). Never mutates.
Exit codes (git-style): 0 in sync · 2 drift detected (act) · 1 error.
Run it after `pull` in CI.

With no target, checks every engine surface; otherwise the named ones.
Targets: reference_lists, data_tables, parsers, feeds, forwarders, dashboards, rule_exclusions, metric_definitions, scheduled_reports, datataps, error_notifications, federation_groups, blacklists, case-stages, case-tags, close-root-causes, connector-allowlist, connectors, environments, idp, jobs, networks, playbook-categories, playbooks, sla-definitions, soc-roles, tracking-lists, visual-families, webhooks
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--out` | string | - | data root directory (default: cwd) |
| `--siem` | bool | false | check only SIEM surfaces (needs only ADC creds) |
| `--soar` | bool | false | check only SOAR surfaces (needs only the AppKey) |

## mitre

Read-only: MITRE ATT&CK coverage (techniques × rule count) across custom + curated rules

```text
secopsctl mitre [flags]
```

```text
Aggregate the MITRE ATT&CK techniques your rules detect into a coverage view —
per technique: how many rules cover it, the tactics involved, and the rule ids.
Custom-rule MITRE comes from the YARA-L meta block (mitre_tactic / mitre_technique);
curated rules carry typed tactics/techniques. Rules with no MITRE meta are reported
under UNMAPPED so coverage gaps are visible. --enabled / --alerting filter custom
rules by deployment state (curated rules are managed at the set level and always
included when selected).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alerting` | bool | false | custom rules: only those with alerting on |
| `--enabled` | bool | false | custom rules: only those with the deployment enabled |
| `--format` | string | - | output: table \| json \| csv (default table; overrides the global --output/--json) |
| `--out` | string | - | write to a file instead of stdout |
| `--type` | string | all | which rules to include: custom \| curated \| all |

## pull

Snapshot live SecOps state to local files (read-only)

```text
secopsctl pull <target> [flags]
```

```text
Pull mirrors live Chronicle state into local files for review under
git. It never mutates the instance.

Targets: rules, reference_lists, data_tables, dashboards, curated, curated_rules, feeds, parsers, rule_exclusions, metric_definitions, scheduled_reports, datataps, error_notifications, federation_groups, forwarders, all
'all' pulls every target in order. --filter applies only to curated_rules.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--filter` | string | - | filter expression (only used by 'curated_rules') |
| `--out` | string | - | output root directory for pulled artifacts (default: cwd) |
| `--with-charts` | bool | false | dashboards: dereference each chart into its inline YARA-L query (heavier; default keeps charts as references) |

**Examples**

```bash
# snapshot detection rules into ./rules
  secopsctl pull rules

  # snapshot everything, then review the diff
  secopsctl pull all && git diff

  # snapshot to a chosen directory
  secopsctl pull reference_lists --out ./mirror
```

## push

MUTATING (guarded): create/disable rules, reconcile config. Dry-run by default

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl push <target> [flags]
```

```text
Push changes to the LIVE tenant. Defaults to a dry run; pass --yes to
actually apply (or confirm interactively). Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 error
(`drift` reports divergence with exit 2 without mutating).

Targets:
  rules-create     create live rules from *.yaral with no companion *.yaml
  rules-update     update live YARA-L text where a tracked *.yaral changed (etag-guarded)
  rules-deploy     reconcile each tracked rule's deployment (enabled/alerting/frequency)
  rules-disable    disable locally-tracked rules with deployment.enabled=true
  curated          reconcile curated/deployments.yaml (enabled/alerting)
  reference_lists, data_tables, parsers, feeds, forwarders, dashboards, rule_exclusions, metric_definitions, scheduled_reports, datataps, error_notifications, federation_groups   reconcile local files to live (create/update; --prune to delete)

Not every surface is prune-eligible; run `secopsctl surfaces` to see which
`--prune` can delete (the rest report orphans but never delete them).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alerting` | bool | true | rules-create: initial deployment alerting state |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only; never mutate (this is the default behavior) |
| `--enabled` | bool | true | rules-create: initial deployment enabled state |
| `--out` | string | - | data root directory the engine surfaces read from (default: cwd; matches pull/drift) |
| `--prune` | bool | false | engine surfaces: also delete live objects with no local file (guarded; a no-op on surfaces without a delete API — see `push <target> --help`) |
| `--rule` | string | - | rules-deploy: limit deployment reconciliation to one rule id, display name, or slug |
| `--rules-dir` | string | - | directory of local rule files (default: <dataRoot>/rules) |
| `--run-frequency` | string | LIVE | rules-create: initial run frequency (LIVE, HOURLY, or DAILY) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | skip the interactive confirmation and apply the change for real |

**Examples**

```bash
# preview creating new rules (dry run — the default)
  secopsctl push rules-create

  # apply for real after reviewing the preview
  secopsctl push rules-create --yes

  # reconcile an engine surface, deleting live objects with no local file
  secopsctl push connectors --prune --dry-run
```
